[00:03] 1694002050486486088: hey, thanks for making the time. can you hear me okay?

[02:28] 6032182271036648443: sure. so we're Quillstack, we're in the saas space. and yeah, we're in the middle of moving to Kubernetes and it forced the whole monitoring question open.
[02:57] 6032182271036648443: the team just mutes alerts at this point because ninety percent of them are noise.
[03:44] 1694002050486486088: that's a really common story. what are you using today?

[04:29] 6032182271036648443: we've also looked at Datazen a bit.
[05:08] 1694002050486486088: got it. and is that something you're actively trying to fix?
[05:46] 6032182271036648443: we moved everything to Kubernetes last year and our old tool just doesn't give us pod-level visibility.
[07:03] 1694002050486486088: got it. and is that something you're actively trying to fix?
[07:20] 6032182271036648443: we've got like 80 microservices now and no real tracing, so debugging cross-service issues is guesswork.
[08:37] 1694002050486486088: got it. and is that something you're actively trying to fix?
[09:14] 6032182271036648443: leadership wants us reporting on SLOs now and we don't have a clean way to measure them.
[09:47] 6032182271036648443: we're locked into an annual contract that auto-renews and it's a fight to get out.
[10:50] 1694002050486486088: makes sense. when you picture this working well, what does that look like?
[11:20] 6032182271036648443: the single-pane thing is really appealing, we're tired of jumping between tools.
[12:22] 1694002050486486088: and what would hold you back from moving on this?
[12:43] 6032182271036648443: we got burned on a migration two years ago so people are nervous about doing it again.
[13:25] 6032182271036648443: the current tool works okay, that's part of the problem, it's good enough to be hard to leave.
[14:34] 1694002050486486088: totally fair. let me show you how a couple of teams like yours handled exactly that.
[15:24] 6032182271036648443: yeah that'd be helpful. timeline-wise we're not in a huge rush but it's on the roadmap.
[16:40] 1694002050486486088: great — here's what I'd suggest as a next step.
[17:21] 6032182271036648443: works for me.
